name: Eliezer
overview: Eliezer is a male member of the tribe of Levi, known primarily as Moses' second son. He was born to Moses and Zipporah during their time in Midian, as indicated by the plural reference to Moses' sons when he left Midian. His identity is rooted in this familial and tribal context within the Old Testament narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliezer means 'G-d is my help,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning tied to divine assistance. This proper name is not recorded as being given directly by God but carries a clear declaration of reliance on God's aid.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Eliezer as the son of Moses and Zipporah. He is also inferred to be an ancestor of Rehabiah, linking him to later Levitical genealogies. Beyond these, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Eliezer's importance lies in his position as part of Moses' family, which played a foundational role in the history of Israel. His birth in Midian during Moses' exile marks a significant period before Moses led Israel out of Egypt. As a Levite and descendant of Moses, Eliezer is connected to the priestly lineage that would influence Israel's religious heritage.
